The historical record shows that the phrase “Let them eat cake” first appears in Jean‑Jacques Rousseau’s *Confessions* (written around 1765), where he recounts a “princess of the blood” replying, “Qu’ils mangent de la brioche.”  Rousseau’s anecdote predates Marie Antoinette’s queenship, and no contemporary source ties the words to her.  Scholars therefore conclude that Rousseau attributed the remark to an unnamed princess—often conjectured to be a royal such as Maria Theresa (though the exact identity remains uncertain).
